title: Dataset Discovery v1 (dataset-discovery-v1)
description: Structural contract for the discovery artifact persisted at knowledge/dataset-candidates.json. It is NOT the model's answer — the Dataset Discovery call is answered against dataset-candidates-v1; this document is what the platform stamps around it: per-source provenance (kind, ref, status, reason, retrievedAt, contentHash, evidenceCount), grounded evidence mentions (evidenceId, kind, sourceKind, ref, name, quote, retrievedAt, contentHash, hashBasis, paperKey, url, indexId) and candidates carrying license/access/authorization state plus task/unit/scale/notes. What is checked: the envelope readDiscoveryArtifact fail-closes on (contract, candidates), the provenance the renderer and the reuse hash dereference (generatedAt, inputHash, sources, evidence), the source/evidence fields the CLI table prints, and per candidate the identity plus the objects the promotion gate and `datasets authorize/acquire/link` mutate (candidateId, name, status, license, access, evidenceIds). What is deliberately NOT checked: that evidenceIds resolve to evidence actually offered, that the candidate name matches its evidence, that relatedPapers came from ProvidedPaperRefs, that a url is backed by a real index hit, or that status/downloadStatus/authorization agree with the access facts — grounding and autonomy rules stay in validateDatasetCandidatesOutput, requiresUserConfirmation and assertCandidateExperimentReady. A candidates array may be empty: nothing grounded is a valid discovery result. The status/acquisition/hashBasis vocabularies are TS consts the collectors grow over time, so they stay plain strings rather than enums copied here, where a new kind would silently start rejecting valid artifacts.
